name: GitHub Releases
description: Publishes a GitHub Release with attached artifacts when a version is cut. The release step lives in the Buildkite pipeline, so it runs only after build and test passed on that commit: the version is bumped from the last tag, the tag is created by CI, the artifacts named by the project's own scripts/release-artifacts.sh are attached, and the release is published with generated notes. No version bookkeeping, and no PAT for a human to paste in.

tagPrefix.description: Prefix for the tags CI creates: the release tag is <prefix><major>.<minor>.<patch>, starting at 0.1.0 and then a patch bump of the newest existing tag.

benefits: Cutting a version is one click - CI tags, packages and publishes
The release can only exist for a commit that passed build and test in Buildkite
Versions bump from the last tag; no version file to keep in sync
Artifacts are named by scripts/release-artifacts.sh, which regeneration never overwrites

emittedFiles.purpose: Release-notes classification (Features / Fixes / Dependencies / Other), consumed by --generate-notes.
The tag prefix, how artifacts travel from the build step, what is genproj-owned vs app-owned, prerequisites, and that the release is not a validator.
Seeded once and never overwritten: names and packages what gets attached (dist/ by default).

pipelineContribution.releaseWhen: buildkite is selected and the branch is the default branch

step.notes: Composed by getBuildkiteTemplateData in src/generator/capability-template-utils.js; the build step gains artifact_paths: in the same function.

notInV1: Giving the release step a manual approval gate: it is automatic, like the deploy step
Making the artifact paths a capability configuration option (they follow the language's output directory; see spec.md §4)
A generation-time GitHub action (there is nothing to provision - the release step is committed as pipeline content; this is why externalServices is empty)
